title: Impersonation during account registration
description: An attacker could impersonate the Homeowner during the account registration process, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the Home Hub system and enrolling cameras/sensors under false pretenses.
assumptions: The registration process relies on credentials that can be compromised or forged.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a reasonable choice for impersonation threats at the ExternalEntity source.

title: Disclosure of personal information during registration
description: Sensitive personal information provided by the Homeowner during account registration (e.g., name, address, contact details) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: The registration process collects PII that must be transmitted to the Home Hub.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a reasonable choice for disclosure threats at the ExternalEntity source.

title: Linkability of registration and device enrollment activities
description: The Homeowner's account registration and camera/sensor enrollment activities could be linked across different interactions, potentially revealing patterns of behavior or location.
assumptions: The Home Hub processes and stores registration and enrollment data that could be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable choice for linkability threats at the Process destination.

title: Linkability of Guest Access Events
description: The Home Hub may log guest access events (timestamp, access code entry) that could be linked to the guest's identity or other activities, potentially revealing patterns of guest presence or behavior.
assumptions: The system logs access events with sufficient detail to enable correlation across time or with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific context may vary based on logging implementation.

title: Detection of Guest Access Activity
description: An external observer could detect that a guest is entering an access code at the Home Hub through observed communication, system responses, or side-effects (e.g., lights, sounds, or network traffic), revealing guest presence without accessing the actual data.
assumptions: The access code entry process produces observable signals (audio, visual, or network) that could be monitored by an eavesdropper.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a general detecting node; specific observable signals depend on the Home Hub's implementation.

title: Disclosure of Access Code Information
description: The temporary access code or guest-related information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure logging, network transmission, or system responses during the access code entry process.
assumptions: The access code or guest data is transmitted or stored in a manner that could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a general data disclosure node; actual risk depends on encryption and storage practices.

title: Linkability of Event Patterns
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could link multiple motion/door/sensor events together to reconstruct detailed patterns of household activity, including occupancy schedules, routine behaviors, and presence/absence patterns.
assumptions: The local event log is accessible to unauthorized parties or the attacker has physical access to the Home Hub/DS1 system.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node L.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context; may need adjustment if specific LINDDUN Pro tree structure differs.

title: Identification of Individuals from Event Data
description: Motion, door, and sensor events could be used to identify specific individuals or their presence in the home, potentially revealing who is present, when they enter/leave, and their movement patterns within the house.
assumptions: Event data contains sufficient detail (e.g., timestamps, sensor locations) that could be correlated with known household members.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node I.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context; may need adjustment if specific LINDDUN Pro tree structure differs.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Log Data
description: The local event log containing motion/door/sensor events could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive information about household activities, occupancy patterns, and potentially security-related events.
assumptions: The local event log is not adequately protected against unauthorized access, or the Home Hub system has vulnerabilities.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node D.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context; may need adjustment if specific LINDDUN Pro tree structure differs.

title: Data Manipulation of Event Log
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could alter, delete, or inject false events, compromising the integrity of the security monitoring system and potentially masking unauthorized access or creating false alarms.
assumptions: The local event log is not adequately protected against tampering, or the Home Hub system lacks proper access controls and audit mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node Dd.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context; may need adjustment if specific LINDDUN Pro tree structure differs.

title: Identification of individuals in camera footage
description: The Home Hub uploads video clips that may contain identifiable information about people in the home environment. This creates a risk that individuals can be identified from the stored footage.
assumptions: Camera captures people who can be visually identified

title: Linkability of video clips to specific individuals
description: Video clips uploaded to cloud storage may be linked to specific individuals or events, potentially enabling tracking or profiling of people in the home.
assumptions: Video metadata or content can be correlated with individuals

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video footage
description: Cloud video storage may be accessible to unauthorized parties, leading to potential disclosure of sensitive home surveillance footage to third parties.
assumptions: Cloud storage has security vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Data manipulation of uploaded video clips
description: Video clips stored in the cloud may be altered, deleted, or tampered with by unauthorized actors or through system failures.
assumptions: Cloud storage lacks integrity controls or is vulnerable to attacks

title: Excessive motion data disclosure to backend
description: Home Hub forwards real-time motion alert data to Mobile App Backend, potentially disclosing personal data about household occupants and their movements. The disclosure may be excessive if the backend receives more granular motion data than necessary for the alert function.
assumptions: Motion data contains personal information about household occupants; the backend is a third party relative to the home environment
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.4 from context [5] as it addresses excessive exposure to external parties

title: Data minimization violation in motion data collection
description: Home Hub may collect and forward more motion data than strictly necessary for the alert function, violating the minimality principle. Only essential motion event metadata should be transmitted, not raw or excessive sensor data.
assumptions: The system collects motion data beyond what's needed for simple alert forwarding
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for data minimization threats

title: Motion alert data integrity compromised in transit
description: Mobile App Backend could receive tampered or altered motion alert data from Home Hub, potentially leading to false security alerts or missed genuine threats. Data integrity must be maintained during the P1→P2 transmission.
assumptions: The communication channel between Home Hub and backend is not fully secured against tampering
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for integrity threats at flow level

title: Linkability of motion notification to homeowner activity patterns
description: The motion-detected notification could be linked to other data about the homeowner's activities, location, or behavior patterns, potentially revealing when and where the homeowner is present or absent.
assumptions: The notification contains contextual data that can be correlated with other data sources about the homeowner.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by context.

title: Disclosure of motion notification to unauthorized parties
description: The motion-detected notification could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission from the mobile app backend to the homeowner's phone, potentially revealing the homeowner's presence or activity.
assumptions: The notification contains sensitive information about the homeowner's presence or activity that should be protected.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by context.

title: Excessive data in motion notification
description: The motion-detected notification may contain more data than necessary (e.g., exact location, timestamp, type of motion), violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The notification includes detailed information that could be reduced to essential alert information only.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by context.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with the cloud analytics vendor may contain patterns or metadata that could be linked with other datasets to re-identify individual users or correlate with other privacy-sensitive information.
assumptions: The vendor may have access to additional data sources that could be combined with this analytics data for re-identification purposes.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro node L.1.1 for linkability threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Analytics Data
description: The cloud analytics vendor may disclose the received analytics data to unauthorized third parties, violating the intended scope of the data sharing agreement.
assumptions: The vendor may have insufficient access controls or may share data with partners without proper authorization.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro node D.1.1 for disclosure threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Transmission
description: Analytics data transmitted from the mobile app backend to the cloud analytics vendor could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during transmission, leading to inaccurate analytics or potential misuse of modified data.
assumptions: The transmission channel may lack adequate encryption or integrity verification mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro node Dd.1.1 for data integrity threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external cloud analytics vendor may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, data minimization, or cross-border transfer requirements are not met.
assumptions: The data sharing arrangement may not have adequate legal safeguards or user consent mechanisms in place.
uncertainty_note: Using standard LINDDUN Pro node Nc.1.1 for non-compliance threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data during retrieval
description: The mobile app backend (P2) retrieves video clips from cloud storage (DS2) for playback. If access controls are insufficient, unauthorized users or systems could intercept or access the video data during transmission or processing, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Access controls on the backend are not properly implemented or are bypassed
uncertainty_note: Using generic D.1.1 node as specific tree node not provided in context

title: Video data reveals identifiable information about homeowner
description: Video clips stored in DS2 and retrieved by P2 inherently contain visual data that can identify the homeowner and potentially other individuals. The process of retrieving and displaying this data creates identifiability risks.
assumptions: Video content contains recognizable faces or identifying features
uncertainty_note: Generic I.1.1 node used; specific tree node not in retrieved context

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: The mobile app backend (P2) may retain video data longer than necessary for the playback purpose, violating the storage limitation principle. Video data should be deleted or anonymized after the playback session is complete.
assumptions: Backend processes do not implement proper data retention policies
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1.4 from retrieved context [4] applies to storage limitation
